Both teams head into the summer now with work to do. Arsenal have to prepare for the additional challenges of the Europa League, while Everton will be bidding to strengthen their squad to prevent another battle against relegation. The action all starts again in August.
Arsenal end the Premier League campaign with an emphatic 5-1 win over Everton at the Emirates Stadium. Despite hammering the Toffees, the Gunners have to settle for a place in the Europa League as Tottenham's win over Norwich City has allowed them to finish in the top four ahead of their North London rivals. Mikel Arteta can still be proud of his team's performance as Gabriel Martinelli put his team ahead from the penalty spot and Eddie Nketiah added a second. The only blemish of the day came before half-time when Donny van de Beek got a goal back for the visitors. However, Arsenal responded with a dominant second-half outing as further strikes from Cedric Soares, Gabriel Magalhaes and Martin Odegaard wrapped up the three points.

Everton pulled themselves back from the brink on Wednesday with a comeback that will live long in the memory against Crystal Palace. The Toffees appeared down and out at half-time trailing 2-0 at Goodison, but Frank Lampard's men mounted an incredible rally in the second half to secure a 3-2 win and their Premier League survival. The club can now relax for one game and play with freedom, but Lampard will be pushing for his team to end the term with momentum to take forward into the new campaign.
Arsenal's hopes of finishing in the top four of the Premier League took a hammer blow after losing 2-0 to Newcastle United on Monday. The Gunners have to beat Everton and hope that Tottenham Hotspur lose to Norwich City on the road. It would be a remarkable turnaround in their fortunes, but Mikel Arteta and his team have to take care of business themselves. Losing back-to-back games will have knocked their confidence and will take a fine effort to claim the three points against a spirited Everton team.

Another brilliant goal doubled their advantage on 33 minutes, when Maddison arched a free-kick from 25 yards out into the top-left corner as Raya was again given no chance. Iheanacho should've killed the game off soon into the second half, when he did so well to outstrength and outpace the two Brentford centre-halves before he lost his composure at the crucial moment, chipping the goalkeeper but watching his dinked effort go wide. Wissa got the visitors back in the game with five minutes remaining with another sublime goal, sending a right-footed drive whistling past Schmeichel. The Danish goalkeeper then made a big save to push a deflected Fosu effort wide, and the Foxes survived some nervy moments in the remaining minutes to secure the victory.

Thanks for joining us for live coverage of Wolves' 1-0 win over Everton in the Premier League.
Those three points for the visitors moves them up to seventh, just two points off the European places. They host Leeds United next, as they look to continue putting the pressure on the teams above them. Another defeat for the Toffees means that they remain 17th, but they are now only out of the relegation places on goal difference. They play Newcastle at home next, as they desperately seek points in their fight against the drop.
The game finishes with the scoreline 1-0 to the visitors. They are full value for the victory, as Everton really struggled to get going and create many clear-cut opportunities. The hosts' task was made harder on 79 minutes, when Kenny received two bookings within a couple of minutes to earn himself an early bath. Wolves held firm in the remainder of the game to give them a hard-fought win.

That massive first victory for Jesse Marsch sees his Leeds side move four points clear of the relegation zone, and a first win in seven games should hopefully spur Leeds on to move further clear of the drop zone. Norwich's late heartbreak, coupled with Watford's corresponding victory over Southampton, means the Canaries are now four points from 19th, and five from safety overall. Time is running out for Dean Smith's side, and quickly.
Raphinha was simply mesmeric in this game, and as well as having a team-leading three shots, seven crosses and winning all of his aerial duels, his four key passes included that late assist to give Joe Gelhardt the winner and set up Leeds' first win in seven games! What a performance from the Brazilian, who was back to his unplayable best today.

That looked to have knocked the stuffing out of Leeds, but up popped the substitute Gelhardt to finish off Raphinha's good work and score a late, late winner for the Whites! Just a second win in 17 Premier League games is the reward for Watford's gritty display today, as they consign their hosts to a third straight defeat and haul themselves closer to safety in the process. Though forced to sit deep for several spells, the Hornets were more threatening in the final third than Southampton, who heavily relied on Ward-Prowse's set-piece mastery to conjure up their few chances. Thanks for joining us for live coverage of the 0-0 draw between Crystal Palace and Manchester City in the Premier League.
The disappointing draw for the visitors means that they fail to extend their lead at the top to six points, and Liverpool can move just one point behind them if they are victorious over Arsenal tomorrow. City will try and get back on track when they travel to Burnley next time out in the league, before a massive showdown with Liverpool at the Etihad Stadium. The point for the Eagles means that they remain in 11th position, and they will host Arsenal in their next Premier League match.
The game finishes goalless after an impressive display from the hosts. They hold firm to deny City the three points, with some excellent defending helped by some toothless attacking from the visitors. The Eagles nearly took the lead early on, after Olise shot just wide after a sweeping attack. The Citizens grew into the game, and almost went in front on 27 minutes when a drilled Cancelo shot from range pinged off the post straight back to Laporte. The French defender hit the rebound first time, but his effort ended up flying over to send the game into the break without any goals. Guardiola's side should've gone in front soon into the second half, when De Bruyne's shot from a tight angle went past Guaita but not the post. Once again, the ball came back into the danger area where Mahrez was waiting, only for Guaita to make an acrobatic save to tip the Algerian's shot over. The best opportunity of the game fell to Silva in the 70th minute, when a teasing Grealish delivery found the Portuguese midfielder a couple of yards out, only for the ball to skim off his foot and go agonisingly wide. City huffed and puffed late on, but Palace remained resolute to see out the remaining minutes and earn a hard-fought point.

City's lead at the top of the Premier League table returns to six points, a lead Liverpool can't cut this week ahead of their EFL Cup final. Champions need to find a way to win when they're not at their best, and Guardiola's men certainly did that. Everton stay 17th, just one point ahead of Burnley. City get back to winning ways with a fluke victory over hardworking Everton! Palace make three changes to their starting 11 from their defeat to Tottenham. Guehi, Schlupp and Mateta come in for Tomkins, Conor Gallagher and Zaha. There are six changes to Norwich from two days ago. Byram, Sorensen, Giannoulis, Lees-Melou, Idah and Tzolis all enter the fray.

SUBS: Martin Kelly, Nathan Ferguson, Luka Milivojevic, James Tomkins, Christian Benteke, Remi Matthews, Jack Butland, Jairo Riedewald.

Things are looking bleak for the Premier League's basement side Norwich after they endured a 5-0 home thumping by Arsenal on Boxing Day. The Canaries have scored just eight goals in their 18 league games so far, and will have no chance of staying up if they can't start finding the net.
Palace's problems with COVID-19 may have contributed to their 3-0 defeat to Tottenham a few days ago, but the Eagles should still be optimistic even with Wilfried Zaha suspended. The Londoners have scored in each of their last eight at Selhurst Park and lost just one of their last nine home games against promoted sides.

City start the new year with a tantalising trip to in-form Arsenal at the weekend, when they can go further clear at the summit of the standings, while Brentford - who remain nine points above the relegation zone - host Aston Villa, and are sure to be buoyed by today's commendable effort.

The champions were off-colour today, and Guardiola will be displeased with some of their imprecise play in the final third, but another three points puts them eight clear at the top heading into 2022. Despite their shortcomings, City controlled possession throughout to rack up their tenth league win in a row - in four of their last five they haven't conceded a goal. Champion form?

City have conceded just 12 goals in 19 previous Premier League outings - three of those coming on Boxing Day alone - so are more than capable of keeping a clean sheet until the final whistle. Therefore, the odds of Brentford now winning their third top-flight home game on the bounce - a feat they haven't acheived since March 1939 - are particularly slim.
For those who feared a one-sided walkover before kick-off, it has been a pleasant surprise to witness a close-fought encounter, with chances at either end. Certainly, the visitors have had most of the ball and could have added to their lead with some more clarity in the final third, but Brentford are holding their own so far - with Toney and company showing no sign of backing down. Burnley have won four of their last seven league games against West Ham (L3), as many as they had in their previous 22 against them. They did lose both Premier League meetings with the Hammers last season, however.

West Ham are flying high in fourth place, currently occupying the final Champions League qualification spot, after downing previous league leaders Chelsea 3-2 in their last top-flight outing.
Burnley have struggled for form throughout the 2021-22 campaign and fell to a disappointing 1-0 defeat against relegation rivals Newcastle United in their last game. The Clarets, who have a game in hand on most of the teams around the bottom of the table, sit three points adrift of safety at the minute, with just 10 points to their name from 14 games.

After a sluggish start, Leicester progressed through the gears today, sealing a much-needed win after a tough week on and off the pitch. Newcastle moved to within three points of escaping the bottom three last weekend, after beating Burnley to secure their first success since the appointment of Eddie Howe. The Magpies' 1-0 victory, courtesy of a goal from top scorer Callum Wilson, ended a run of 14 Premier League matches without a win. However, ahead of kick-off today, they have the worst away record in the top flight - picking up only three points from seven previous road trips this term.
Following a run of just one win from their last six games, Leicester have slipped into the bottom half of the Premier League table, and are now afflicted by an illness outbreak at the club. Thursday's 3-2 defeat at Napoli saw the Foxes demoted to the Europa Conference League, but they can at least concentrate on domestic concerns until February. Having conceded at least twice in each of their last five league games at the King Power - their worst such run since 1964 - the Midlands side will hope to fare better at the back today.

Elland Road explodes with relief, as Leeds finally secure a third win of the Premier League season in such nailbiting fashion. Bielsa's side were marginally the better over the course of the 97 minutes, though rarely looked like breaking the deadlock due to a worryingly blunt attack. Only Guehi's misfortune in giving away a stoppage-time spot-kick offered them the chance to steal all three points and close the gap to Palace down to a single point. Brentford's first win in six sends them rocketing up the table into twelfth, and seven points above the relegation zone. In the process, they leapfrog 14th-placed Everton, who are now winless in their last seven games. Worrying signs for Rafa Benitez, and their performance today won't fill their fans with much hope that they will improve any time soon.
His winner may only have been his only shot of the entire match, but Ivan Toney today showed how important he is to Brentford all over the pitch. Involved in a game-high 23 duels, nine of which came in the air, the Bees striker also chipped in with four clearances, and won three fouls. An all-action performance from a striker proving that he is one of the best in the league on his day.
And that's that! Not the most memorable game, but an important one for Brentford who pick up their first win in six matches! It was Ivan Toney's penalty, awarded after a VAR review, that separated the two sides, but Everton didn't create anywhere near enough in the way of chances to truly trouble the home side, who held on for their first victory at the Brentford Community Stadium since August!

With that win, Southampton leapfrog Watford in the table and are now two places above them, in 14th. For the Hornets, they're just three points off the bottom three, and with their next five games being against Arsenal, Manchester United, Leicester, Chelsea, and Manchester City, it'll be a near-miracle if they haven't slumped further down the league by the end of that period.
Although their attack was the difference in this game, it's worth noting how well Mohammed Salisu did at the back for Southampton in this game. Although he lost control of Ismaila Sarr later in the second half and was booked, he still finished the match with a team-high four tackles, six clearances and three interceptions, showing that he was imperative in ensuring that the Saints' forward players were never without the ball for too long.
It's all over, and Southampton have their second win of the season! As with their first against Leeds, the Saints were the better team for large spells of that match, and although Watford did improve in the second half, their potency let them down and they couldn't find an equaliser as the away side held out for the win. West Ham's victory takes them up to seventh in the Premier League table, meanwhile Leeds, who remain winless after six games, have dropped into the relegation places and languish in 18th. Marcelo Bielsa's side need to find a win from somewhere, and if they tail off as poorly as they did today, they may continue searching for some time yet.

Newcastle beat West Ham in their opening Premier League match last season, winning 2-0 at London Stadium. They haven’t won on matchday one in consecutive Premier League seasons since beating Wigan Athletic in 2006-07 and Bolton Wanderers in 2007-08.
West Ham, meanwhile, go with a familiar starting eleven: their 4-2-3-1 today is entirely comprised of players who were at the club last season.
